title: Smoke cleanup can kill unrelated concurrent Nextra instances
test: tests/smokePackaged.test.js: 'cleanup kills the tree of the executable the smoke launched and leaves a Nextra instance started during the run alone' (runs the real node scripts/smoke-packaged.js with the real process listing against a stand-in executable: a node copy under <tmp>/.../caxa/applications/nextra-<id>/0 that runs as caxa stub -> server), plus 'selectCleanupTargets picks the processes the run owns and their descendants, never another instance or a pre-existing process' and 'cleanup kills the launched child through its handle, the processes the run owns and their descendants, and nothing else'
proof: Holds. Cleanup SIGKILLed every process whose command line matched the shared caxa nextra- pattern unless its PID was in the pre-launch baseline. Before the fix the script-level test failed on the unchanged script: the test started a decoy (node with a command line under <tmp>/.../caxa/applications/nextra-decoy/0) as soon as the smoke printed 'Starting packaged executable', i.e. after the baseline; the stand-in failed the package-info stage; the old cleanup then killed the stand-in stub and server and also the decoy: 'the smoke killed a Nextra instance it did not launch (PID 30408)'. The selectCleanupTargets and cleanup unit tests failed with 'smoke.selectCleanupTargets is not a function' and, for cleanup, with the child never killed through its handle (killSignals [] instead of ['SIGKILL']). Fix (scripts/smoke-packaged.js): cleanup(run) no longer matches patterns. selectCleanupTargets({ records, ownedPids, knownProcesses, baseline, exitedPids }) returns the owned PIDs (launched child, the server verified at readiness, an adopted replacement), every process seen in the run's tree before (PID -> command line, remembered at readiness, at adoption, before the shutdown request and in each shutdown/cleanup listing) and their current descendants by parent PID. Never the run's, and never walked through: a process with the same PID and command line as in the baseline (the baseline is now every process, PID -> command line, so it protects processes, not numbers), a known PID that now runs another command line (reused), and a process holding the launched child's PID after its exit was observed. A PID nobody holds still links its children (Windows keeps a dead parent's PID; on macOS a reparented process stays known through knownProcesses). The child is killed with child.kill('SIGKILL') while the monitor has no exit record; the other targets by PID; the runner's own PID is never a target. After the fix the decoy survives (isAlive true), the stand-in stub and server are dead, the smoke exits 1 for the failed stage and logs 'Killing the processes of this run: <stub PID> (...), <server PID> (...)'. Residual: a dead owned PID reused within the run by a process with an identical command line would still count as the run's; no creation-time check was added.

title: Smoke process enumeration fails open, so leftover-process checks can pass without checking anything and CI can hang
test: tests/smokePackaged.test.js: 'a process list that cannot be read before the launch stops the smoke before it launches anything' (real script, PATH emptied so neither powershell.exe nor ps can start), 'listProcesses throws when the process list cannot be read, instead of returning no processes', 'a process list that cannot be read in cleanup is a cleanup error, and the child is still killed through its handle', 'a simulated packaged run with real processes passes, logs the launched executable exit, and the smoke ends on its own'
proof: Holds. listProcesses() returned [] on a spawn error, a non-zero status, empty stdout, ENOBUFS or unparsable JSON, and cleanup then reported nothing. Before the fix the script-level test failed on the unchanged script: with an unreadable process list the smoke launched anyway, failed verification ('The process list came back empty, so the ready server (PID 37792) cannot be tied to the launched executable'), skipped the cleanup shutdown, killed nothing, and then never exited because the still-running child kept the event loop alive: 'exit null SIGKILL after 20229 ms' (the test's 20 s limit), stub and server left running until the test removed them. The listProcesses unit test failed with 'Missing expected exception: win32', the cleanup one with 'no cleanup error'. Fix (scripts/smoke-packaged.js): listProcesses({ platform, spawnSyncImpl }) passes the spawnSync result through readProcessList, which throws 'Process enumeration failed: ...' on result.error (ENOENT, ENOBUFS), a non-zero status or a signal (with stderr), no output, a parse failure or zero records; maxBuffer is raised from 8 to 64 MiB. main() takes the baseline (takeProcessBaseline) before the spawn and throws 'Could not take the pre-launch process baseline, so the packaged executable was not launched. ...' without launching. Every later listing (readiness, recovery adoption, shutdown wait) now fails its stage instead of seeing nothing. In cleanup an enumeration failure is a cleanup error, and the child is still killed through its handle; if it does not exit within 5 s after SIGKILL that is a failure too and the handle is unref'd, so the smoke always ends. After the fix the script-level test exits 1 in about 0.1 s with nothing launched; the simulated run with real processes (stub -> server -> replacement child, real Win32_Process listings) passes and the smoke process ends on its own with code 0.

title: Graceful-shutdown stage never asserts process exit, and cleanup silently force-kills survivors
test: tests/smokePackaged.test.js: 'the requested exit of the launched executable passes the shutdown stage, in the shutdown phase set before the request', 'a non-zero or signalled exit of the launched executable in the shutdown phase fails the shutdown stage', 'a /healthz timeout is not a stop: the shutdown stage fails when the port never refuses connections', 'a process the run owns that is still alive at the shutdown deadline fails the shutdown stage', 'after a handover in recovery the shutdown stage waits only for the adopted replacement, and says its exit code is not observable', 'cleanup reports the processes that survived graceful shutdown as a failure, then kills them', 'cleanup reports a cloudflared the run started, or any new one, and never one that ran before', plus unit tests for evaluateShutdown and classifyShutdownProbeError
proof: Holds. checkGracefulShutdown ignored the shutdown answer, counted any /healthz error including the 1 s abort as stopped, and never looked at the child's exit; cleanup force-killed survivors before its stale check. Before the fix, on the unchanged script: a child exiting with code 1 or by SIGTERM after the shutdown request, a /healthz that only times out, and a media worker of the run still alive after the exit all passed the stage ('the stage passed' where a failure was expected); the requested exit happened in phase 'stages' (actual 'stages', expected 'shutdown'), so the monitor classified it as unexpected; the handover case did not log the unobservable exit code; cleanup returned no error for survivors ('Missing expected rejection.') or for an owned cloudflared ('no cleanup error'). Fix (scripts/smoke-packaged.js): checkGracefulShutdown checks ownership, lists the run's tree, then setPhase('shutdown') and only then sends the POST; it is not raced against the monitor's unexpected promise. The pure evaluateShutdown({ childExit, survivingOwnedPids, postResult, deadlineExpired, portDown }) passes only a 2xx answer (or a connection reset or closed by the server, when the owned exit then followed), a child exit in 'shutdown' with code 0 and no signal (non-zero or a signal fails), or an exit already recorded in 'recovery'/'post-recovery' (neutral, logged as 'replacement exit code not observable'), a port that refuses connections, and no surviving owned process. waitForShutdown waits within one deadline (15 s) for the child's 'exit' (skipped after a recovery handover), a /healthz probe classified by classifyShutdownProbeError (ECONNREFUSED or ECONNRESET is down; an AbortError or anything else is not), and an empty owned tree; plain timers, no timer left behind. cleanup(run) sets 'cleanup' first; when the stage sent its request, any owned process still alive is recorded as 'Cleanup found processes that survived graceful shutdown: <pid> (<command>), ...' before the kill; the cloudflared check (any cloudflared not in the baseline, which includes the run's own) now runs on the listing before the kill, so killing cannot hide one. After the fix all these tests pass, and the simulated real-process run logs 'Graceful shutdown: launched executable exited (code 0, no signal) in phase 'shutdown'.' One existing test fixture was changed: 'a simulated packaged run passes every stage in order, each destructive request right after an ownership check' kept listing the launched processes after its fake server shut down; it passed only because the stage never checked for live processes, so its shutdown hook now also empties the process list (one line). PS1 (Q-001): scripts/smoke-packaged.ps1 is referenced by no workflow, package.json script or doc (both workflows run node scripts/smoke-packaged.js), so per the Q-001 default it was left unchanged and is recorded as retired. Not run: the approval-gated packaged smoke against a real Nextra.exe / Nextra-macos-arm64 (no package built in this lane).
